verdicts.quote: “Almost all Plaid API endpoints require a client_id and secret… These may be sent… in the headers PLAID-CLIENT-ID and PLAID-SECRET.”
verdicts.reason: Plaid’s API uses a static client_id + secret for app authentication, which fits the “API key” category for a multi-tenant toolkit.

verdicts.quote: “Wait for OAuth approval from Plaid, which can be tracked on the OAuth institution page.”
verdicts.reason: Keys are self‑serve, but meaningful Production/OAuth use requires approval and completing compliance steps (e.g., security questionnaire), matching “app_review.”

verdicts.quote: “Possible values: assets, auth, balance, balance_plus, beacon, identity, identity_match, investments, investments_auth, liabilities, payment_initiation, identity_verification, transactions”
verdicts.reason: Docs show many products/endpoints across major domains (accounts, transactions, identity, investments, liabilities, payments, etc.), so breadth is “broad.”

verdicts.quote: “Plaid offers two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers: The Dashboard MCP server is a remote MCP server hosted by Plaid.”
verdicts.reason: Plaid publishes/hosts an MCP server and also ships a local MCP server in their official toolkit; this is an official MCP.

verdicts.quote: “The Plaid Sandbox is a free and fully‑featured environment for application development and testing. Sandbox API keys can be obtained in the Plaid Dashboard.”
verdicts.reason: Buildable now via self‑serve Sandbox and full docs; caveat is Production/OAuth requires approval (see OAuth guide), so “ready_with_caveats” with blocker=app_review.
